memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then they said, 'Let's call the young woman and ask her about it.' So they called Rebekah and asked her, 'Will you go with this man?' 'I will go,' she said." - Gen 24:57-58 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Now comes a turning point that rests on Rebekah's own choice. Her family calls her and asks plainly, "Will you go with this man?" Her answer is simple and brave: "I will go."

Think about what she is agreeing to. She would leave her home, her parents, and everything familiar to marry a man she has never met, in a land she has never seen. It would take real faith and courage. Yet she says yes without hesitation, trusting that God was in it.

Her answer echoes the faith of Abraham himself, who long ago left his country at God's call (Heb 11:8). God often invites us to say "I will go" before we can see the whole road ahead. Following Him usually means trusting Him with the unknown.

Is God asking you to step out into something new — a change, a calling, an act of obedience that means leaving comfort behind? You may not see how it all ends. But like Rebekah, you can say "I will go," trusting the God who leads. Faith is not the absence of the unknown; it is willingness to move forward while holding God's hand.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is God asking me to step into something new and unknown?
2. Can I say "I will go" while trusting God with the details?
3. What comfort might I need to leave behind to follow Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me Rebekah's willing heart to say "I will go" when You call, even into the unknown. I trust You to lead me every step of the way. Amen.
